item.title: Creative Australia: International Engagement Fund (October 2026 round)
item.description:
Organisation: Creative Australia

Location: International, with a confirmed overseas partner.

Award: AUD 5,000 to 30,000. No application fee. No formal matching requirement, but assessment explicitly weighs diversity and scale of income and co-funding, including earned income, grants, sponsorship and in-kind contributions.

Duration: Activities must not exceed two years from the proposed start date; supported activity must fall between 1 July 2026 and 1 July 2028.

Deadline: 13 Oct 2026

Supports reciprocal international exchange between Australian practitioners or organisations and confirmed overseas partners, which makes it the right instrument for co-hosted convenings, labs and cross-border programme partnerships rather than one-way touring. Supported activity types are creative collaboration and development, cultural exchange and knowledge sharing, and labs and practice-exchange models, mapping closely onto media arts residencies, art-and-science research exchanges and digital culture symposia. Eligible costs include artist fees, travel, accommodation, production expenses, marketing, access costs, and childcare or carer support. International organisations are eligible where the project benefits Australian artists or creative workers, and a confirmed international partner is mandatory and must confirm participation in writing. The reciprocity requirement is substantive: the strongest applications embed mutually beneficial exchange rather than simply presenting an Australian artist abroad. Creative Australia's published assessment feedback notes top-ranked applications foregrounded First Nations self-determined or diasporic-led activity and demonstrated sector-wide impact. It is competitive: 157 eligible applications in the March 2026 round yielded 33 grants, about a 21 percent success rate. Contemporary music practitioners are excluded and directed to Music Australia programmes. Closes 13 October 2026 at 3pm AEDT.

item.title: Creative Australia: Arts Projects for Organisations (September 2026 round)
item.description:
Organisation: Creative Australia

Location: Activity may take place nationally within Australia, internationally, or online.

Award: AUD 20,000 to 100,000. No matching or co-financing requirement. No application fee. Organisational administrative costs should generally not exceed 10 percent of the total project budget or the application becomes less competitive.

Duration: Activity must last no longer than two years from the proposed start date; the project must commence after notification and within one year of it.

Deadline: 01 Sep 2026

Creative Australia's principal open-round project grant for arts organisations and the most directly relevant Australian scheme for mounting festivals, exhibitions and public programmes. The guidelines explicitly list festivals, productions, exhibitions, performances, touring, publishing, recording, collaborations, research and community engagement as supported activity. Organisations may propose either a single project or an entire programme of projects, which can extend to a full artistic programme for a given calendar year or longer, so this can function as de facto annual programme funding. The category is artform-agnostic and routinely supports media arts, digital culture, experimental sound and art-and-science work; activity delivered online is explicitly permitted. NOTABLE: international organisations are eligible where the project demonstrably benefits practising Australian artists, their work, or Australian audiences, so a non-Australian festival can apply if it is programming Australian artists. The applicant must be a legally constituted entity: incorporated association, company limited by guarantee, or government statutory authority. Registration in the Application Management System must be completed at least one business day before the closing date. The round closes 1 September 2026 at 3pm AEST.

item.title: BigCi Environmental Awards 2026
item.description:
Organisation: Bilpin International Ground for Creative Initiatives (BigCi)

Location: Bilpin, New South Wales, Australia, on the edge of Wollemi National Park in the UNESCO World Heritage-listed Greater Blue Mountains, about 1.5 hours from Sydney. Open to Australian and international artists.

Award: Two awards, each of AUD 5,000 prize money plus four weeks of free residency at BigCi, guided walks in the surrounding national parks and research assistance for the project. AUD 40 entry fee, non-refundable and payable with the submission.

Duration: Four-week residency at BigCi per winner

Deadline: Closed 02 Aug 2026

BigCi's Environmental Awards are an annual prize for work that engages with the environment, open to Australian and international artists working in visual art, installation, multimedia, performance, literature, music, photography, filmmaking and curating. TWO WINNERS each receive four weeks of free residency at BigCi plus AUD 5,000 in prize money. BigCi sits on the edge of Wollemi National Park in the Greater Blue Mountains, an hour and a half from Sydney but geologically another world; winners explore the UNESCO World Heritage-listed Wollemi, Blue Mountains and Gardens of Stone National Parks on guided walks and are given research assistance relevant to their projects. At the end of their residencies they present the work at the BigCi Open Day. JUDGING: three independent judges, Lea Kannar-Lichtenberger (Australia), Brian Wallace (China) and Dan Gottlieb (USA). APPLICATION: an online submission form (Wufoo) linked from the awards page, with a non-refundable AUD 40 entry fee paid at the time of submission. KEY DATES: submissions close 2 August 2026; winners announced 22 August 2026. Enquiries via the contact form at bigci.org/contact.
